question: Which statement best describes id and class?
options: The boolean hidden attribute removes an element from rendering and the accessibility tree entirely — equivalent to display:none semantically. Use it for content that isn't currently relevant (a collapsed panel). Note: hidden='until-found' is a newer variant that keeps content findable by in-page search.

style holds inline CSS for a single element (best avoided in favor of classes, and incompatible with strict CSP). title supplies advisory text shown as a native tooltip on hover — but it's not reliably accessible to keyboard or touch users, so don't rely on it for essential information.

lang declares the element's language so screen readers pronounce it correctly and tools can translate it; set it on <html> and override on any element whose language differs. dir sets text direction — ltr, rtl, or auto — essential for right-to-left scripts like Arabic and Hebrew.

id is a document-unique identifier used for anchoring (#section), label/for associations, ARIA references, and getElementById. class is a space-separated list of names, reusable across many elements, used as CSS and JavaScript hooks. ids must be unique; classes are for grouping.
explanation: id is a document-unique identifier used for anchoring (#section), label/for associations, ARIA references, and getElementById. class is a space-separated list of names, reusable across many elements, used as CSS and JavaScript hooks. ids must be unique; classes are for grouping.

data-* attributes let you attach arbitrary custom data to any element without inventing non-standard attributes. JavaScript reads/writes them via element.dataset, where data-user-id becomes dataset.userId (kebab-case → camelCase). They're the standard way to pass per-element state from markup to scripts.
